I don’t know all the details, but that’s something that happens every single week in the NFL.”Hurts had informed the Eagles’ medical staff that another player’s cleats struck his calf during Philadelphia’s October 4 game against the Los Angeles Rams. He received treatment on October 8 and practiced fully before the team travelled to London.An ultrasound on October 10 detected a superficial blood clot in his left calf. After medical evaluation, doctors cleared him to play against Jacksonville the following day. Hurts completed the game, throwing for 220 yards and a touchdown, although Philadelphia lost 19-17.A follow-up ultrasound on October 14 then revealed movement in the clot. The Eagles announced on October 15 that Hurts would miss their next game while doctors determined his treatment. Why Patrick Mahomes says football cannot come before players’ healthFor Mahomes, the situation goes beyond losing a fellow quarterback to injury. He pointed out that NFL players have families and lives outside football, even when their commitment to the sport demands so much from them.“We love it, and we love playing football, and we love being out there every single week, and we give everything we have, but at the end of the day, we’re human beings, and we have families and stuff that we want to be there for a long time,” Mahomes said on the 96.5 The Fan podcast.He also expressed hope that treatment would allow Hurts to recover and eventually return to football. Mahomes praised Hurts as one of the players who makes the NFL better.The Eagles and Hurts’ agent, Nicole Lynn, provided a more detailed medical update on October 19. They confirmed that further testing had identified deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, meaning blood clots had reached both lungs.The statement described Hurts as clinically stable and said doctors expected a full recovery without long-term effects. His treatment involves blood thinners, which prevent him from participating in contact activities while he takes the medication. NFL faces fresh scrutiny over Jalen Hurts’ medical treatmentHurts’ diagnosis has also prompted questions about how the situation unfolded before the London game. On Oct. 21, NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said the league welcomed a review after the NFL Players Association called for an investigation.Speaking at the NFL’s annual fall meeting, Goodell defended the medical protocols followed by the Eagles and said the league’s chief medical officer had reviewed the process.Hurts has been placed on injured reserve, and reports indicate he could miss the remainder of the 2026 season. His exact return date remains uncertain.Mahomes’ comments underline the concern surrounding a diagnosis that has taken one of the league’s leading quarterbacks out of action. articles.summary: Allen Bailey, 'defensive end' que impresionaba por su físico, pasó la mayor parte de su carrera en los Kansas City Chiefs
articles.body: Allen Bailey, el conocido como 'Hulk' de la NFL por su espectacular físico (1,91 metros y 131 kilos), fue encontrado muerto por su esposa en su domicilio de Florida. Se desconocen las causas del fallecimiento del exjugador de 37 años, aunque su familia informó a TMZ que creen que su muerte se debió a causas naturales. Allen Bailey comenzó su trayectoria en la NFL con los Chiefs en 2011 y pasó la mayor parte de su carrera como 'defensive end' en la franquicia de Kansas City. "Nuestros corazones están con su familia y nuestras oraciones los acompañan. Es una edad demasiado temprana, obviamente. Era uno de mis jugadores favoritos, un gran muchacho. Lamento profundamente que esto le haya sucedido", lamentó Andy Reid, entrenador de los Chiefs. Bailey disputó sus primeras ocho temporadas con los Chiefs. En 2018 protagonizó la mejor temporada de su carrera. "Cuento esta anécdota cada año: Allen Bailey fue la primera persona que vi al entrar al vestuario tras el draft (de 2017). Vi a Allen Bailey y pensé: 'Esto ya no es la Big 12'. Fue algo surrealista verlo allí... Obviamente, es terrible recibir esta noticia. Fue un gran compañero; era uno de esos jugadores que mantienen unido al equipo. Hacía jugadas clave. Quizás no era una superestrella, pero era el tipo de jugador que hacía que todo funcionara. Estamos rezando por su familia", recuerda Patrick Mahomes, que compartió dos años vestuario con Bailey. Allen Bailey concluyó su trayectoria en Atlanta, donde disputó sus dos últimas temporadas con los Falcons. "Es terrible, sobre todo teniendo en cuenta todo lo bueno que hizo. Tiene familia, y es una situación muy triste. Sé que su padre también murió siendo joven. Es algo que te deja una sensación terrible cuando le sucede a alguien tan joven", apuntó Andy Reid

articles.body:
This year seems to be a little better for fantasy football tight ends . And it's an important part of the process for fantasy managers . And here is a look at the NFL start 'em, sit'em for the tight end position in Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season.

There's no surprise at the top of the list. Nobody needs to be told to start Brock Bowers and George Kittle with their matchups. However, some may hesitate with Trey McBride. Don't make that mistake.

Start 'em: Cardinals' Trey McBride vs. Broncos

Yes, the Broncos have a beastly defense. And they seem to be finding their way , according to denverbroncos.com.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"Defensively, we were magnificent," Broncos head coach Sean Payton said following the Broncos' win over the Seahawks. "I don't know how many times we hit the quarterback. We got three takeaways. We felt like that was going to be a big deal in this game, being smart with the football. Two years in a row, we beat the [reigning] Super Bowl team, and that's not easy to do."

However, McBride is a locked-in starter. It's not because the Cardinals will necessarily score a lot of points against the Broncos. But he will get targets. And he will catch passes. He's a top-five NFL player in that regard.

The best thing about McBride from a fantasy football standpoint is he takes his job seriously for 60 minutes, regardless of the score, according to azcardinals.com.

"One thing about me, I'm going to play to the end," McBride said. "I'm going to play until the game is over, and I'm going to do that every single week."

McBride is getting tons of attention from defenses. But he said he works hard through double teams.

"I've got to get open," McBride said. "I've got to give Jacoby a reason to throw me the ball. I expect them to double me. Kind of makes it a little more challenging."

The Broncos will make life tough for McBride. But he should be able to succeed.

Start 'em: Packers' Tucker Kraft at Lions

Kraft still hasn't had that breakout game this season, but this could be the week. He's further removed from last year's injury, and the Lions offer a soft defense.

Still, the Lions enter with confidence , coming off a bye, according to detroitlions.com.

"I think we are improving in areas, and I think there's still a lot of room to improve," Lions head coach Dan Campbell said. "But I do think we're beginning to figure out who we are a little bit here. And we're getting some help. We're getting a little bit of help back in some areas. So, we've just got to continue to improve. That's this league, man. You're not trying to make this big jump every week. You just have to try to incrementally improve and find a way to win that game."

But Matt LaFleur knows the value of a guy like Kraft. And this seems like a good spot for him to employ higher usage against a division rival. LaFleur had some praise for Kraft recently, according to Packers.com.

"I think Tuck's what we wanna be about," LaFleur said. "I think he shows up every day and puts 100% into this thing. And he does a great job. He's obviously earned the respect from his teammates, being voted the captain. He does things the right way. You can't have enough guys like Tucker Kraft."

Start 'em: Lions' Sam LaPorta vs. Packers

Yes, we expect this game to be a shootout. That bodes well for both Kraft and LaPorta. Over the last two games, LaPorta has 13 catches for 172 yards and two scores. He has become quite a weapon in a diverse offense.

And the good thing is the Packers can't take everybody away. They will have to focus on Amon-Ra St. Brown and the receiving prowess of Jahmyr Gibbs. That means LaPorta will get his chances.

The only negative thing for LaPorta these days is his contract situation , according to ESPN.

"I don't know if it's truly off the table, but I think there's certainly a stalemate right now and I'm really giving the reigns to my agent Jack Bechta," LaPorta said. "He's been handling it with the front office, and all the advice he's given me so far is just that we haven't come to terms yet. That's about it."

Sit 'em: Giants' Isaiah Likely at Texans

It's hard to bank on Likely against a Texans defense that seems to have found its footing. Plus, there are question marks at the quarterback position. McCarthy threw for 243 yards in the fourth quarter, giving him a leg up over Jameis Winston. Perhaps.

Head coach John Harbaugh had some good words for McCarthy, according to ESPN.

"I thought he came in there and did a heck of a job given the circumstances," Harbaugh said.

Likely could thrive with either quarterback. He has had 17 catches for 193 yards and three touchdowns over the last two weeks. But that's why he's risky this week. The Texans will focus on taking him away. That will open the door more for Malik Nabers.

articles.body:
It's another week for fantasy football managers to make key decisions. And that includes the quarterback position . Also, let's look at the start 'em and sit 'em for fantasy defenses and special teams for Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season.

There are some easy calls on the start list this week because of matchups. And let's get right to one of the NFL's premier defensive units.

We know what the Cardinals bring to the field. They have a high-volume passing attack with an emphasis on Trey McBride and Michael Wilson. But the Broncos had a lot of answers last week against Jaxon Smith-Njigba and the Seahawks. Head coach Sean Payton certainly likes where his defense is , according to denverbroncos.com.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"Defensively, we were magnificent," Payton said following the Broncos' 17-14 overtime win against the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks. "I don't know how many times we hit the quarterback. We got three takeaways. We felt like that was going to be a big deal in this game, being smart with the football. Two years in a row, we beat the [reigning] Super Bowl team, and that's not easy to do."

Quarterback Bo Nix, who has made life harder for the defense with his erratic play, said that unit made the difference against the Seahawks.

"They were fantastic," Nix said. "They contributed to that win probably bigger than anyone else, any group for sure. We don't win that game without them."

And fantasy managers can count on defensive coordinator Vance Joseph.

"[Defensive Coordinator] Vance [Joseph] is always elite at what he does," linebacker Justin Strnad said. "There were so many calls tonight that he put us in the perfect position. Great calls. He does it week in, week out."

Don't even bat an eye. The Texans still have the defensive dogs. And they will show out and show up this week.

The Giants have a shaky offense with major questions at quarterback. And anybody who thinks JJ McCarthy is going to continue playing as he did in relief of Jameis Winston will get a big dose of reality.

The Texans didn't sniff a sack against Trevor Lawrence and the Jaguars in Week 6. That will change this week. Look for them to fantasy feast on Winston or McCarthy.

Head coach DeMeco Ryans said quick decisions by Lawrence made things tough on the defensive front to get pressure, according to Texanswire.com.

"From the pressure standpoint, the ball was out pretty quickly," Ryans said. "I thought Trevor [Lawrence] did a good job of getting the ball out quick. They had a really good game plan for our guys. The field, the surface, was slippery for both sides. I don't think their defenders got any sacks either. It was hard to get that footing and get downhill in the rushes. I give credit to Jacksonville, first and foremost, for the game plan and how they executed."

But the Texans need to clean up missed tackles.

"When we secure, you have to wrap up and truly put your body on people," Ryans said. "You have to wrap up, and you have to run your feet. You really have to grab, wrap, squeeze, and really run your feet. We weren't running our feet much in that game. We were just arm tackling and playing against those backs.

"Again, this week versus the Giants backs, they have two good physical backs as well. We have to improve it very quickly."

Other good defenses to start: Minnesota Vikings versus Colts, New York Jets versus the Dolphins, Cleveland Browns at the Titans.

Sit 'em: Philadelphia Eagles vs. Cowboys

Don't buy this logic: The Eagles have a good defense and the Cowboys' offense is struggling. Both are true, but from a fantasy standpoint it's a false narrative. The Cowboys are going to jack up the Eagles' defense this week.

Sure, the Eagles believe in their defense. And that unit played well against the Panthers, according to PhiladelphiaEagles.com.

"I thought (our) defense played a heck of a game," quarterback Tanner McKee said. "It's really hard to win in the NFL only putting up 14 points. And obviously we put that on ourselves as an offense. I put that on myself as a quarterback to create more explosive plays and put more points on the board."

The Eagles have a flaw that will show up against the Cowboys.

"I think we're lacking consistency," linebacker Zach Baun said after the loss. "We were playing well coming into this game, and then there was good times. And there was also bad times in this game. We just got to stay consistent and execute.

"Whether our offense is doing good or they're not doing so hot, our defense always strives for perfection and always tries to get our offense back on the field and give them opportunities to score."

It's best to avoid a fantasy matchup against Dak Prescott and those killer receivers.

Other defenses to avoid: Cincinnati Bengals at Ravens, Las Vegas Raiders versus Rams, Green Bay Packers at Lions.

Is your fantasy team bad? Are you hoping to swing some trades to save your season?

You've come to the right place—the fantasy football trade value chart is here to help. Let's salvage that season, together.

Players who would be ranked in the 51-100 range have a descending trade value between six and two. Players below the top-100 range have a value of one. Trade values are based on PPR scoring, so adjust according to your league's particular scoring settings. May the fantasy points be with you!

The buy-low window on Malik Nabers has obviously slammed shut, but the question now is what sort of prices you should be offering, or expecting, if he comes up in trade talks.

In the past three weeks, he's been one of the truly elite receivers in fantasy, with a whopping 35 targets—and 23 receptions—in the past two weeks alone. The fact that he hasn't been touchdown reliant to post elite numbers is a strong argument in favor of his current form being sustainable.

The move to Jameis Winston didn't hurt Nabers' production, and when JJ McCarthy entered Sunday's game in the fourth quarter, he targeted Nabers five times, completing four passes to the star wideout for 95 yards across five series.

That was garbage time, of course—though the Giants shockingly had a chance to tie the game down the stretch, nearly erasing a 24-point deficit—but it was a strong indication that Nabers' fantasy ceiling may actually rise if McCarthy is given the starting job going forward (and is given a full practice week to work with the ones).

You shouldn't be expecting JSN or Puka prices for Nabers, but he's slowly inching his way toward the second tier of top wideouts. At this point he feels basically quarterback-proof. Big things are coming for New York's top wideout.

Another player trending in the right direction, in a big way, is Drake Maye. He's thrown for 10 touchdowns and just one interception in his past three games (and rushed for one as well), just got AJ Brown back (though losing Romeo Doubs will hurt) and has a fairly manageable schedule until later in the season.

If you are selling, you can probably get a very nice price for Maye given the hot streak. He probably can't keep up this level of production consistently. But he's once again reminiscent of the player who had a breakout season in 2025, and that player finished as the No. 2 quarterback.

There's little reason to believe he won't be somewhere in that ballpark again this season after his recent three-game burst.

articles.title: 5 Way-Too-Early 2027 NHL Draft Predictions
articles.summary: October is far too early to make any predictions for the upcoming NHL entry draft, but we're going to do it anyway.
articles.body:
October is far too early to make any predictions for the upcoming NHL entry draft, but we're going to do it anyway.

For public scouts, the draft season is a year-long rollercoaster of myriad leagues and players and narratives. Everyone is in love with Landon DuPont's play right now, and rightfully so, but at the moment there doesn't appear to be much consensus across the board after him. Maybe that will crystallize as time goes on, but right now so much is in the air.

And rightfully so! We haven't seen enough of these players to make a full and coherent judgment yet. That's what makes it fun and exciting.

Here's a quick prediction for you before we get into the real ones, though, because this isn't a hot take—it's ice cold. It's going to be another down year for the USNTDP. There's maybe two players who are first round-level right now. USA Hockey really needs to figure that out, and fast.

1. Landon DuPont Will Fall Out of the Top Spot

Every guy who is considered the consensus first overall going into the season inevitably falls out of favor at some point. It happens with fans, it happens with public scouting services. It probably happens with teams, but we don't have access to their information. It's a long year and attention spans are very short these days.

DuPont is off to a good start with the University of Michigan, after two excellent seasons with the Everett Silvertips of the WHL. He's currently sitting at six assists in five games—which makes complete sense, because DuPont's biggest strength is distribution.

He's absolutely incredible at getting the puck precisely where it needs to be at any given moment; his vision allows him to break down opponents' play to identify weaknesses. He's also an incredibly deceptive player, able to surprise guys going up against him with how he finds teammates and how he gets them the puck.

Across a long and difficult hockey season, consistency in a top-ranked player can be a double-edged sword. People start to question you; are they really seeing what they think they're seeing? What if this other guy who has surged late is actually better? So I do think we'll see DuPont fall back behind a few others in conversation, at least for a while, though I couldn't tell you when.

But I don't think he'll stay behind them in the end.

2. We'll See More NCAA Commits from Top CHL Prospects

The CHL-to-NCAA pipeline looks like it's here to stay, and will continue to grow as a prominent development path. Players will rev up their pre-draft careers with their CHL teams, get the consistency of those close-to-professional-comparable season lengths under their belt, and then transfer to the NCAA for post-draft years that they would otherwise spend as overagers on a CHL team to sand off any rough edges that their NHL organizations deem obstacles. It feels like one that should be effective, and thank god. NHL teams need to get better at the development process.

When it was initially introduced, there was some mild speculation that the new CHL-NHL agreement might help curb the flow of players to the NCAA. It doesn't appear that's going to be the case. The agreement only affects one player from each organization, and it only applies to 19-year-old players. It also only applies to players drafted in the first round. For the most part, guys affected by that rule are not guys who are going to go from the CHL to college hockey anyway.

There are, of course, the rare cases of players who make that transfer for their draft year itself. We saw it last year with both Gavin McKenna and Keaton Verhoeff. This year, as far as top prospects go it's only Landon DuPont (Sammy Nelson, at the University of Notre Dame, comes from the USNTDP).

3. It's Going to Be A Center-Heavy Draft

Center. Centre. However you spell it, there are going to be a lot of them selected in the first round.

Multiple of the (very few) draft lists out right now have nearly half the slots filled by either natural centers or players who can play or have played both center and wing. We're going to see a lot of them go pretty high. It's still extremely early, but let's take a look at a few guys who fit this mold.

Jaxon Jacobson — Brandon Wheat Kings center Jacobson is considered undersized at 5'10", but his skill level is high enough that his height probably won't matter. His Draft-1 year point totals landed at 85 in 63 games; right now he's at 9 in the first 11 games of the season. Highlights of his game include his playmaking and speed.

Alexis Joseph — Saint John Sea Dogs center Joseph didn't overly impress at this year's Hlinka Gretzky Cup; that said, the pieces for a top-10 talent are all there if he keeps driving forward and puts them all together. His puckhandling in particular shines. He had 60 points in 54 games last season; currently he is at 10 points in 11 games.

Carter Meyer — Quebec Remparts center Meyer joined the QMJHL this season from the USNTDP (something we are seeing happen more and more often lately). He played with the U18 squad as a Draft-1 player and was one of their best guys, intelligent and hard working and a heck of a lot of fun to watch. You can't really compare USNTDP scoring to QMJHL scoring, but so far this year he has 12 points in his first 10 games.

There are so many more. We'll get to them in our next look at the overall class.

Flyers Regretting Their Offseason Moves 🤦‍♂️

Quick Predictions on Biggest Storylines 🔮

4. Vancouver Will Miss First Overall Again

Sorry, Canucks fans. The hockey gods just aren't on your side.

I'm not going to try to predict how the Canucks' season is going to go; I'm not clairvoyant. But other people smarter than me have, and most of them project the Canucks finishing at the bottom of the Pacific Division and in the bottom three of the NHL. That's not ideal; even if it does give them better chances at the top pick, it gives them even greater chances at getting the second or the third.

And sure, at some point the draft balls have to start falling their way. But they've been on such a rough run of draft lottery results that it's hard to envision them getting the first overall pick.

And hey: even if they do, Landon DuPont is not going to be a franchise-changer for them. They're in far too much of a hole offensively. If the Canucks were looking for a top prospect that would drag them into a better timeline, last year was the time for it. Which brings me to our final prediction.

DuPont could be a game changer for the right team. After him, though, much like last year it's a lot of swinging on potential.

From a team standpoint, that's a double-edged sword. On the one hand, if you're in the mix for a lottery pick, you're pretty much always looking for a prospect who can help tilt the ice in your franchise's direction. If you miss out on that top slot and DuPont is off the table, your next choices are players who will almost certainly need a few years to develop.

On the other hand, it's an opportunity to truly shape your prospect pool in a specific way by looking for player types that your franchise is lacking. In drafts where there are several consensus strong prospects at the top of the pool, aiming for a particular player mold over simply drafting the best player available typically comes with significant opportunity cost. Not only are you taking a chance on potential, you're leaving that BPA on the table for someone else to draft.

But when there's not a strong top pool and everyone is pure potential, you've got more freedom to play around.

articles.title: Biggest Sleepers at Every Position for Week 7 Fantasy Football 2026
articles.summary: In Week 7, fantasy football managers have to work around bye weeks for Josh Allen, James Cook, Trevor Lawrence, Bhayshul Tuten, Parker Washington and Jayden Daniels. On top of that, wide receiver Davante Adams could miss the rest of the regular season with a hamstring tear.
articles.body:
In Week 7, fantasy football managers have to work around bye weeks for Josh Allen, James Cook, Trevor Lawrence, Bhayshul Tuten, Parker Washington and Jayden Daniels. On top of that, wide receiver Davante Adams could miss the rest of the regular season with a hamstring tear.

So, this week's sleepers list features a mobile quarterback with an appealing rushing matchup, running backs who can make a significant impact in the running and passing games, high-upside rookie wideouts and a tight end who may soak up some of Adams' targets in the Los Angeles Rams offense.

Unlike previous weeks, Week 7 selections start with a Thursday night pickup, giving fantasy managers a chance to get a quick jump on opponents.

Here are eight sleeper options—all available in at least 50 percent of leagues, according to FantasyPros ' roster consensus percentages.

QB Malik Willis at New York Jets (21 Percent Rostered)

If the Miami Dolphins get their first win of the season, it'll be because they ran the ball effectively against the New York Jets' 23rd-ranked run defense, which is 19th in yards allowed per carry.

Miami can lean on running backs Ollie Gordon II and Jaylen Wright, along with quarterback Malik Willis, to get the job done on the ground.

In the Dolphins' last outing before their Week 6 bye, Willis logged eight carries for 74 yards and a touchdown. If that's a sign of what's to come, he could post a similar stat line in a favorable matchup for Miami's run game.

Furthermore, Willis may have Caleb Douglas back in action for the first time since Week 2. The rookie third-round wideout caught five passes for 94 yards in his regular-season debut.

If Willis is part of the Dolphins' ground game plan, he has QB1 upside.

QB Tanner McKee vs. Dallas Cowboys (3 Percent Rostered)

In his third career start—and his first of the season—Tanner McKee threw for 215 yards and a touchdown, which isn't too bad against the Carolina Panthers' 19th-ranked pass defense.

Fantasy managers would want more from him as a starter, and they could see better numbers against the Dallas Cowboys.

Dallas is allowing the fifth-most fantasy points to quarterbacks. Remember, two weeks ago, undrafted rookie signal-caller Jalon Daniels had a solid showing against the Cowboys, throwing for 189 yards and a touchdown. McKee isn't as mobile as Daniels, but he has wide receivers to attack Dallas' secondary.

With McKee under center, wideout DeVonta Smith and tight end Dallas Goedert topped 60 receiving yards. The Eagles' passing game could find a rhythm under the Monday Night Football lights. Dallas has allowed at least one passing touchdown in every game this season.

RB Tyrone Tracy Jr. at Houston Texans (10 Percent Rostered)

Last week, the New York Giants turned their backfield pecking order upside down. None of their running backs handled more than six carries, and Cam Skattebo didn't touch the ball. Najee Harris expressed dissatisfaction with his role , and the Giants released him days later.

Tyrone Tracy Jr. led Big Blue's backfield with eight touches and saw three targets as the Giants tried to mount a comeback from a 24-point deficit. Without Harris in the rotation, Tracy's workload could increase.

Tracy lost his way in the Giants' backfield platoon after a rough preseason in which he fumbled and missed a blocking assignment , but he's at least the No. 2 tailback ahead of Devin Singletary going into Week 7. Given Skattebo's benching last week, the third-year pro could have the biggest workload.

It's worth noting that Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten caught four passes for 48 yards and two touchdowns against the Houston Texans last week. Tracy could take on a sizeable role on the ground and in the short passing game.

RB Roschon Johnson vs. New England Patriots (9 Percent Rostered)

A rare Thursday night sleeper. Insert Roschon Johnson into your lineup. He's the Bears' No. 2 running back, with Kyle Monangai sidelined by thumb and toe injuries.

Monangai has missed the last two games, and in those contests, Johnson has recorded 18 carries for 57 yards and a touchdown and caught seven passes for 68 yards. Even more encouraging for Johnson's role in the ground attack, he's seen only two fewer goal-line touches (five) than lead running back D'Andre Swift over the last two weeks, per FantasyPros .

The New England Patriots aren't a plus matchup for running backs, but they've given up a fair amount of receiving yards to running backs. In Week 5, the Las Vegas Raiders' trio of tailbacks, Ashton Jeanty, Mike Washington Jr. and Dylan Laube, racked up 71 yards on seven catches.

Johnson is a sneaky RB2 play who can get you an early lead in matchups this week.

WR Ja'Kobi Lane vs. Cincinnati Bengals (24 Percent Rostered)

Rookie third-rounder Ja'Kobi Lane returned from wrist surgery and made an immediate impact, catching four passes for 40 yards. He could continue to see more targets than Rashod Bateman, who exited the previous game with a shoulder injury.

Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter is optimistic that Bateman avoided a major injury, but Lane has more upside, and his productive outing with backup quarterback Tyler Huntley is an encouraging sign for his short-term fantasy value.

The Cincinnati Bengals' pass defense has improved, but the unit is still in the middle of the pack in yards allowed (18th) and yards allowed per pass attempt (16th).

Lane has short-term WR3/flex appeal and could see his role grow as the season progresses. Make sure he's not available in your league, even if you don't plan to start him this week.

WR Ted Hurst III at Carolina Panthers (4 Percent Rostered)

On Wednesday, Tampa Bay Buccaneers wide receiver Emeka Egbuka popped up on the injury report with a concussion and a foot injury. Even if he passes concussion protocol, the second-year pro may be limited by his foot issue.

Rookie third-rounder Ted Hurst III is an intriguing WR2 or WR3/flex option, pending Egbuka's status. He could see more targets out wide against the Carolina Panthers, who are without their starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson. In its last two games, Carolina has allowed 75-plus receiving yards to four different wide receivers.

Also, Buccaneers starting quarterback Baker Mayfield could be back from a dislocated thumb. He took part in a full practice on Wednesday.

Regardless of Egbuka's status, Hurst is in a favorable spot, as the Buccaneers will likely have to score at a high rate to keep pace with the Panthers' fourth-ranked scoring offense.

TE AJ Barner vs. Kansas City Chiefs (12 Percent Rostered)

Given that the Seattle Seahawks hired former San Francisco 49ers tight ends coach Brian Fleury, AJ Barner has had a disappointing start to the season.

After catching 52 passes for 519 yards and six touchdowns last year, he hasn't carved out a consistent role in the Seahawks' passing attack.

Yet there's hope Barner can gain momentum this week. He's caught at least three passes in three of his last four outings and has a matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs, who allow the third-most fantasy points to tight ends.

The Chiefs will allocate heavy coverage to star wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, so other pass-catchers will need to win their one-on-one matchups in the passing game.

If Barner doesn't break out against a defense vulnerable in the middle of the field on National Tight Ends Day , it may not happen this season.

TE Colby Parkinson at Las Vegas Raiders (4 Percent Rostered)

The Los Angeles Rams must compensate for the loss of wide receiver Davante Adams, who will miss six to 10 weeks with a hamstring tear. Puka Nacua will likely see double-digit targets for the foreseeable future, though the Rams have featured multiple tight ends in their offense with a healthy receiver corps.

Without Adams, the Rams' tight ends should be more involved in the aerial attack. With Terrance Ferguson on injured reserve, you can choose between Tyler Higbee and Colby Parkinson. Both should be active in two-tight-end sets.

Last week, Parkinson saw six targets, two more than Higbee, catching five passes for 31 yards and a touchdown. Coming off a season with career highs in catches (43), receiving yards (408) and touchdowns (eight), he's likely ahead of Higbee in the pecking order.

Working in Parkinson's favor, the Las Vegas Raiders have struggled to cover tight ends, tying for sixth in fantasy points allowed to players at the position. Las Vegas has given up at least eight catches to a team's tight end group in three of its last four games.

Fantasy points scored against statistics are provided by FantasyPros .

Maurice Moton covers the NFL for Bleacher Report. You can follow him on Twitter @MoeMoton .

articles.summary: Week 7 is set to kick off with Thursday night's matchup between the New England Patriots and Chicago Bears.
articles.body:
Week 7 is set to kick off with Thursday night's matchup between the New England Patriots and Chicago Bears.

While the Bears recently got star quarterback Caleb Williams back in the lineup, the Patriots just placed receiver Romeo Doubs on injured reserve with a shoulder injury. Unfortunately, Doubs' injury won't be the only one with which fantasy managers will need to be concerned this week and moving forward.

Jalen Hurts will miss the rest of the season as he undergoes treatment for blood clots. Davante Adams will miss between six and 10 weeks with a hamstring injury.

In addition to the latest rash of injuries, managers will have to deal with the Buffalo Bills, Jacksonville Jaguars, Los Angeles Chargers, and Washington Commanders being on bye this week.

Naturally, managers will be looking for sleepers and waiver-wire targets to help fill the void.

Here, you'll find updated rankings for Week 7, a cheat sheet for value plays, and a look at some top options who may still be available on the waiver wire. All rankings and picks are based on point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco 49ers

Waiver-Wire Target: Mike Washington Jr., RB, Las Vegas Raiders

The Las Vegas Raiders have a solid starting running back in Ashton Jeanty, but the second-year man hasn't been healthy all season. He's dealing with a foot injury now and appeared to be far less than 100 percent during Sunday's offensive slugfest with the Buffalo Bills.

While Jeanty led the Raiders in carries, it was rookie Mike Washington Jr. who led the team in rushing yards. He averaged 4.8 yards per rush against Buffalo, far exceeding Jeanty's 2.2 yards-per-carry average.

While Washington's Week 6 performance yielded just six fantasy points, he could see a bigger offensive role moving forward.

The Raiders will face a middling Los Angeles Rams defense (!6th-most fantasy points allowed to opposing RBs) this week. Washington is rostered in just 37 percent of fantasy leagues.

Report reveals list of next NFL international locations

AP: Jordan Elliott Released After Pulling Out Gun

Waiver-Wire Target: Omar Cooper Jr., WR, New York Jets

New York Jets rookie receiver Omar Cooper Jr. spent four weeks on injured reserve with an ankle injury. However, he was activated ahead of Week 6 and immediately delivered a breakthrough fantasy performance.

Cooper caught six passes for 103 yards and a touchdown against the rival New England Patriots, rewarding fantasy managers with 22.3 points. He probably won't replicate that production in Week 7, but Cooper is still a must-add in most formats.

The Jets will host the Miami Dolphins this week. The Dolphins have surrendered the third-fewest fantasy points to opposing receivers, though that's largely because teams have gotten ahead early and leaned on the run against Miami—the Dolphins rank 29th in net yards per pass attempt allowed.

Cooper can do some early damage in Week 7 and is worth flex consideration. He's certainly worth claiming for his long-term upside, and he's rostered in just 23 percent of leagues.

*Fantasy scoring and roster information from FantasyPros .

articles.title: Re-Ranking Ashton Jeanty, 2nd-Year NFL RBs After Week 6
articles.summary: The 2025 NFL draft was a good one for teams needing a running back—or so it seemed.
articles.body:
The 2025 NFL draft was a good one for teams needing a running back—or so it seemed.

In last year's draft, two running backs were selected in the first round, with two more taken in the top 40. Over two dozen backs were drafted overall. The class appeared to offer everything: an elite prospect in Ashton Jeanty, high-end talent and considerable depth.

So far, though, the class has not lived up to those expectations.

Some backs from the Class of 2025 have impressed, at least in stretches. Arguably, the biggest flashes have come from the fourth-to-last running back selected. But the class has yet to produce a clear star, and questions remain about nearly every back in the group.

Now, just over 20 weeks of NFL action isn't enough of a sample size to pass final judgment on those young runners' careers. But what we can do is take what we've seen so far and re-rank those backs based on talent, production and potential.

This top 10 looks considerably different from the original draft order.

When the Miami Dolphins used a sixth-round pick on Ollie Gordon II last year, expectations were modest.

Maybe Gordon could become something of a "thunder" complement to De'Von Achane's "lightning" in the backfield, but no one expected Gordon to be the lead back in Miami's backfield.

But that was before Achane tore his ACL. Now, it's Gordon's backfield for the rest of the season.

To be clear, Miami's offense has struggled overall. The Dolphins rank 28th in yards per game but ninth in rushing yards per game, and Gordon has contributed to that success.

The Oklahoma State product has averaged 5.0 yards per carry, recorded his first career 100-yard rushing game in Week 4 against the Minnesota Vikings and scored a touchdown in three straight games.

If that continues the rest of the season, Gordon is going to have a role in the Dolphins offense in 2027—even with Achane back on the field.

9. Jacory Croskey-Merritt, Washington Commanders

Jacory Croskey-Merritt was a great story last year—the seventh-round pick out of Arizona who went from being the last running back drafted to starting seven games for the Washington Commanders as a rookie.

In his first career start last year against the Los Angeles Chargers, the 5'11", 208-pounder carried the ball 14 times for 111 yards and two touchdowns. By the end of that first season, he had surpassed 800 yards on the ground, averaged a respectable 4.6 yards per carry and found the end zone eight times.

Things haven't gone as well in 2026. His yards per attempt have dropped by a full yard, and he is currently on injured reserve with a groin injury. He has also offered little as a receiver, with just 14 career receptions.

But Croskey-Merritt has shown he can at least be part of a committee attack in the backfield as a between-the-tackles grinder.

Not that long ago, Cam Skattebo would have ranked far higher on this list.

After showing some flashes as a rookie, the 2025 fourth-rounder entered Year 2 as the lead back for a young and exciting Giants offense.

Many expected a breakout 2026 season from Skattebo, but his ball-security struggles have complicated that outlook.

Ball security hasn't been his only concern; his rushing efficiency has also declined. In five starts as a rookie, he had two games with at least 100 total yards, scored five touchdowns and averaged 4.1 yards per carry.

In six games this year, Skattebo has one 100-yard performance and one touchdown while averaging just 3.6 yards per carry. Ball security has also been a concern, and he received no touches in Week 6.

R.J. Harvey of the Denver Broncos is one of the harder backs to slot on this list.

On one hand, Harvey has played relatively well to this point in his NFL career. He averaged only 3.7 yards per carry as a rookie but finished with almost 900 total yards and 12 touchdowns, taking over as Denver's lead back after J.K. Dobbins got hurt. He's an excellent receiver out of the backfield, and there's an argument that he's the best back on the Broncos' roster.

But Harvey's usage suggests Broncos head coach Sean Payton doesn't view him as an every-down back. He has never had 20 carries in a game, and while his yards-per-carry average is up slightly from last season, it remains underwhelming.

Harvey's NFL future appears to be as a passing-down and change-of-pace back, so it's hard to rank him any higher than this.

When the Cleveland Browns drafted Ohio State's Quinshon Judkins early in Round 2 last year, the expectation was that he would quickly become a reliable, productive every-down back. He demonstrated that skill set with both the Buckeyes and Ole Miss.

However, returns so far have been mixed.

There have been bright spots—chief among them a 23-carry, 110-yard effort against the Minnesota Vikings last year. Cleveland's offensive line has also struggled, but Judkins averaged just 3.6 yards per carry before breaking his leg and dislocating his ankle last season.

This year, the 22-year-old has struggled to generate explosive gains, averaging just three yards per carry.

Judkins still has the talent to run between the tackles, get outside and contribute as a receiver. For now, though, his production has fallen short of expectations.

Some may be surprised to see Chicago Bears running back Kyle Monangai ranked this high. But a few years from now, he could be viewed as the biggest running back steal of the 2025 NFL draft.

Monangai may be behind D'Andre Swift on Chicago's depth chart for now, but he has already demonstrated the ability to carry a run game.

In the season opener, Monangai had 100 yards and a touchdown on just 10 carries. In a Week 4 win over the New York Jets, he had a whopping 30 carries for 146 yards and a pair of scores.

Mind you, this came after a rookie season in which the Rutgers product averaged over five yards per touch, flirted with 950 total yards and scored five touchdowns.

Monangai is averaging a gaudy 5.4 yards per carry this season, and his 2.6 yards after contact per attempt is tied for fourth in the NFL.

His production supports a higher ranking than his draft position might suggest.

In his second season, Bhayshul Tuten appears to be coming into his own with the in-form Jacksonville Jaguars.

After relatively modest numbers as a rookie, the 23-year-old is taking advantage of a larger role with the Jags. He's averaging 4.1 yards per carry, chipping in 9.7 yards per reception and has found the end zone four times in six games. At his current pace, he would end his second professional season with over 1,450 total yards.

At 5'9" and 209 pounds, Tuten isn't the biggest back, but he runs with power. He currently ranks sixth in the league in both yards after contact per attempt (2.5) and broken tackles (8).

The Jaguars may be using Tuten as part of a two-headed backfield with between-the-tackles bruiser Chris Rodriguez Jr., but Tuten has shown the talent and versatility to be a lead back. He's also playing a major role for a Super Bowl contender.

3. Omarion Hampton, Los Angeles Chargers

Omarion Hampton has had little opportunity to establish a rhythm.

When the 23-year-old was drafted 22nd overall last year, it was with the expectation that he would be the Chargers' lead back from the jump. He was widely considered a first-round talent after a wildly productive two-season stretch at North Carolina.

An ankle injury sidelined Hampton for almost half his rookie season, but he was effective when available. He averaged 4.4 yards per carry, scored five touchdowns and contributed just under 82 total yards per game.

Then 2026 rolled around, and the wheels came off.

The winless Chargers are a mess, and Mike McDaniel's decision to use a three-back committee has done little to help Hampton find his groove.

Hampton has exceeded 15 carries just once this season, while his yards-per-carry average has dropped by nearly a full yard.

The talent is there, but the situation is a nightmare.

2. TreVeyon Henderson, New England Patriots

This is another ranking some may find puzzling. After all, TreVeyon Henderson has just 225 total yards after five games this season. He's averaging over a yard less per carry than he did as a rookie.

Much has been made of the pass-blocking deficiencies that have stopped Henderson from claiming the lead back role in Beantown.

But as his 39-yard touchdown scamper in his first game of 2026 demonstrated, the Ohio State product has a gear no other back in these rankings possesses. He's a threat to take it to the house every time he touches the ball.

As a rookie, Henderson averaged over five yards per carry. He caught 35 passes, topped 1,100 total yards, scored 10 touchdowns and had two games with a pair of touchdown runs over 50 yards.

Durability is a legitimate concern. But from a pure talent standpoint, there isn't a better back in the Class of 2025.

After piling up a jaw-dropping 2,739 total yards two years ago at Boise State on the way to finishing as the runner-up for the Heisman Trophy, Ashton Jeanty was universally considered the top running back in his draft class.

No one batted an eyelid when the Raiders took the 22-year-old sixth overall.

Despite getting hit in the backfield more often than not as a rookie, Jeanty still topped 1,300 total yards, scored 10 times and caught 55 passes. On a better Raiders team in 2026, he was expected to take a step forward in Year 2. Instead, his production has declined.

The Boise State product isn't doomed to a disastrous season after six weeks, but there's no denying he has struggled this year. He is averaging 3.2 yards per carry and hasn't had a 20-yard run yet this year.

This writer isn't ready to drop Jeanty from the top spot just yet, but he has shown nothing to indicate he's the kind of explosive bell-cow back who merits such a high draft pick.

And the gap between him and the rest of last year's draft has evaporated.

articles.title: Bleacher Report's Expert Week 7 2026 NFL Picks
articles.summary: In Week 6, the Cleveland Browns, Tennessee Titans, and Pittsburgh Steelers all trailed by double-digit margins in the second half and still won, covering the point spreads. Those were among the most topsy-turvy finishes from last weekend.
articles.body:
In Week 6, the Cleveland Browns, Tennessee Titans, and Pittsburgh Steelers all trailed by double-digit margins in the second half and still won, covering the point spreads. Those were among the most topsy-turvy finishes from last weekend.

Analysts Gary Davenport , Brad Gagnon , Kris Knox , Moe Moton , and Brent Sobleski , along with editors Wes O'Donnell and Ian Hanford , took a moment to reflect on another tough week. They're back for a potential get-right slate, although the panel did go 4-0 on lone-wolf picks in Week 6.

This week's games have thin point spreads, with only one team favored by more than a touchdown. Let's see how our experts broke down the games.

First, take a look at the standings against the spread. Moton extended his lead with a 9-5 record last week. As a lone wolf, one analyst took big swings on a couple of home underdogs to make up ground in Week 7.

Lines are from FanDuel as of Wednesday, Oct. 21, at 4 p.m. ET. Check FanDuel for the latest odds info. Information on public betting trends is courtesy of the Action Network . ATS records are provided by Team Rankings .

New England Patriots (4-2) at Chicago Bears (4-2)

Chicago is back in a groove following a strong performance in Atlanta and now gets to host the banged-up Patriots traveling on short rest. Behind a vulnerable offensive line, Drake Maye could be in a lot of trouble against a defense that generated three takeaways in Week 6.

So far this season, underdogs are 5-1 ATS in Thursday night games, though this is more than a trend pick. Drake Maye has his swagger back, throwing for 10 touchdowns and an interception in his last three games.

Maye gets a favorable matchup against the Bears, who gave up 367 yards and two touchdowns through the air in a 31-7 Week 5 loss to the Green Bay Packers and allowed Michael Penix Jr. to throw for 225 yards and three touchdowns last week. Meanwhile, Chicago faces New England's stingy fifth-ranked scoring defense.

In a battle between quarterbacks from the 2024 draft, this should be a close one. It's a field-goal game either way. We could get a push here, but don't hesitate to take the points.

Patriots: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell

Pittsburgh Steelers (4-2) vs. New Orleans Saints (2-4)

I never know what to do with games overseas, but I'll back the more consistent team here. The Saints looked better against the Giants last week, but they also almost let go of the rope against J.J. McCarthy in the second half. The Steelers' offense has been middle of the road through six weeks of the season, but New Orleans' defense has struggled and will continue to do so here. Pittsburgh leans on Jaylen Warren and the run game to get the cover here.

I have absolutely no faith in the New Orleans Saints' ability to play disruptive defense or stop the run. The Saints head into Week 7 ranked 28th in yards per carry allowed, 29th in yards allowed, and 31st in points allowed.

However, I also don't trust the Pittsburgh Steelers' ability to play well offensively in back-to-back games away from home.

The Steelers should have an easier time moving the ball against the Saints' sieve of a defense than they had against the Buccaneers early last week. However, I think some red-zone struggles and a few late miscues will open the door for Tyler Shough to mount his own comeback.

Steelers: Davenport, Hanford, Moton, O'Donnell

Tampa Bay Buccaneers (1-5) at Carolina Panthers (3-2)

It's possible Baker Mayfield returns this week, but even if he doesn't, Jalon Daniels has shown the ability to compete every week. Carolina is playing well thanks to a surging Bryce Young, but these divisional games this time of the year tend to stay tight. The Panthers hang on to win, but it'll be by a field goal or less.

Whether or not Baker Mayfield plays this weekend, I give the Panthers the edge, especially with Bryce Young playing at a high level.

It remains unclear how well Mayfield can grip the ball, which is especially concerning given his tendency to overthrow receivers. If Jalon Daniels starts, Tampa Bay's limited passing production raises doubts about its ability to exploit a Panthers pass defense ranked in the league's bottom half.

Buccaneers: Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell

San Francisco 49ers (6-0) at Atlanta Falcons (2-4)

Is it possible that the Niners will falter on an East Coast trip to play at 1 p.m.? Will the team finally reach a tipping point amid its seemingly never-ending run of injuries? Those are legitimate concerns, but I'm still backing San Francisco. Brock Purdy is my MVP pick through six weeks, and the Niners look like Thanos with the Infinity Stones right now—inevitable.

The 49ers had to hold off the Washington Commanders' late-game Monday night rally, and they travel east on a short week with a banged-up wide receiver corps that may be without Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles). If this were Madden, the difficulty setting would be turned up to the max for the 49ers.

San Francisco defensive coordinator Raheem Morris could get revenge on the team that fired him at the beginning of this year, but it'll be a tight game. Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson Jr. wear down the 49ers' run defense to put them on upset alert.

Falcons: Gagnon, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Cincinnati Bengals (3-2) at Baltimore Ravens (4-2)

Lamar Jackson's ankle injury leaves his availability uncertain, but even if he sits, the Ravens are the pick here.

Cincinnati had an extra week to prepare, but Zac Taylor's record as head coach off a bye (3-4) isn't great, largely because the Bengals regularly get road trips like this coming out of the off week. His road record is worse.

The Ravens get after Joe Burrow, lean on Derrick Henry and win by a field goal.

I'm going to assume that Lamar Jackson is back in the lineup for the Baltimore Ravens this week. Having Jackson back will allow the Ravens to pressure the Cincinnati Bengals' new-look defense—which has been solid overall but still ranks 30th in yards per carry allowed.

However, the Bengals are coming out of their bye and should have a plan for stopping Derrick Henry. They can field the sort of aerial attack that will give Jesse Minter's defense trouble. Baltimore's defense has been great against the run, but Zac Taylor doesn't really believe in establishing the run anyway.

While the Ravens' pass defense looked terrific for most of last week, it's been decidedly average for most of the season. Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins are anything but average, and I think they'll outshine Jackson in his first game back from injury.

Ravens: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, O'Donnell

New York Giants (3-2-1) at Houston Texans (2-4)

It looks like the New York Giants will go with quarterback J.J. McCarthy this week, which doesn't inspire a lot of confidence, given his NFL track record. In an early season that has been defined by monumental upsets, though, I have a hard time backing the Houston Texans with a line this large, regardless of which Giants QB they're facing.

Houston's defense has looked nothing like the top-tier unit it was a year ago. There have been times when it's felt like the Texans merely suggest that the opposition stay out of the end zone rather than stopping them.

The Texans have been quite good offensively. However, I think that John Harbaugh will have a plan for C.J. Stroud that is far more effective than whatever strategy he employed against Tyler Shough last week.

Houston should get its first home win of the season here, but Harbaugh's squad should keep it relatively close.

This past Monday morning, "Quit Playing Games (With My Heart)" by the Backstreet Boys came on '90s radio. It felt fitting after the Giants disappointed at home against the Saints following my enthusiastic endorsement in these picks. The close final score doesn't change my view: Big Blue should have leaned on the running game all day.

Instead, the Giants' offensive approach left me questioning how they intend to use their backfield. After backing them last week, I'm not making the same pick again.

This is a poor matchup for a Giants team in the midst of an offensive identity crisis. The Texans are 0-3 at home this season but have won two straight games, including an international thriller against the division-rival Jaguars last week.

Houston's offense is starting to show signs of life, and I expect the defense to deliver its best performance of the year. That should be enough for a double-digit win and a cover.

Giants: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, Sobleski

Miami Dolphins (0-5) at New York Jets (2-4)

Prior to their Week 6 bye, the Dolphins played a couple of one-score games against solid opponents. Now they appear due to finally get their first win of the season with two weeks to prepare for a Jets team that has failed to score 20 points in three consecutive games. It's hard to see Gang Green winning this by more than a field goal, if they win it at all.

The Jets are the better of these two bad teams. New York's pass defense has been among the league's best. The run defense hasn't been as strong, but Miami's offense isn't strong enough to succeed if it's forced to be one-dimensional.

The Dolphins had their bye week to prepare for the chance to get their first win, but I like New York to bounce back from its Week 6 loss and win at home by a touchdown.

Dolphins: Davenport, Gagnon, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell

Cleveland Browns (4-2) at Tennessee Titans (1-5)

The Browns are in first place, but their underlying numbers raise questions. Their point differential of minus-16 is the worst of all division leaders. Cleveland has a bottom-five offense in both yards and points per game, and no team has allowed more sacks (24). The Titans have struggled, but the Browns haven't played as well as their record suggests.

The pressure is off the Titans after winning their first contest this past weekend, which is fortunate because quarterback Cam Ward will likely have a difficult outing against the Browns defense. Cleveland's defense may not be ranked highly from a statistical standpoint, but the unit has played with an aggressive and opportunistic approach all season.

The Browns wouldn't be leading the AFC North right now without their defense dictating terms. If the first six weeks have been any indication, the Titans offense isn't prepared to handle a quality opponent.

Indianapolis Colts (2-4) at Minnesota Vikings (5-0)

The Indianapolis Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard, but that won't improve Daniel Jones' passing efficiency or patch up the team's 27th-ranked scoring defense. By the way, cornerback Sauce Gardner won't play in this game because of a calf strain.

The Minnesota Vikings had extra time to prepare for this matchup, off a bye week. Also, Kyler Murray looked sharp in the Vikings' last outing, throwing for 229 yards and a touchdown with an 80 percent completion rate. Assuming Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson are healthy, Minnesota beats the struggling Colts by at least a touchdown.

Sunday's outing against the Vikings is the Colts' last gasp before their season could unofficially come to a close. Chris Ballard's ouster as general manager became inevitable after Indianapolis' embarrassing loss to the previously winless Tennessee Titans. Head coach Shane Steichen could be next.

Furthermore, the Colts could quickly become sellers at the trade deadline if something doesn't change over the next three weekends. Meanwhile, the Vikings are undefeated and at home. However, they're facing a desperate team that will likely bring its best to the table.

Vikings: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell

Denver Broncos (4-2) at Arizona Cardinals (2-4)

The Cardinals are 2-4 this season, with both wins coming at SoFi Stadium. At home, they average just 14 points per game and haven't won since Week 2 of last season.

That's nine straight home losses. Arizona could threaten a backdoor cover, but a turnover could also stretch a one-score Denver lead to two scores.

Denver's offense is struggling badly, but its defense is good enough to justify laying these points on the road.

At this point, no one should expect much from the Broncos offense. Bo Nix and Co. simply aren't good. Denver relies too heavily on its defense to keep it in games and hopefully pull out a victory late in the process.

Conversely, the Cardinals continue to compete despite obvious roster deficiencies. Arizona has scored 18 or more points in all but one game this season. The Broncos have failed to score 18 points in two of their last three games.

Broncos: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell

Los Angeles Rams (2-4) at Las Vegas Raiders (3-3)

Why lay this many points on the road against a Raiders team that just covered the same spread against Buffalo? The Bills aren't 2-4, and I don't see enough here to justify backing the Rams at this number.

Vegas also gave the Chiefs all they could handle at Allegiant Stadium a few weeks ago. Meanwhile, when we last saw the Rams, they were losing at home as 12.5-point favorites to the Cardinals.

The scrappy Raiders win outright—and a wobbly season for the Rams comes off the rails.

The Raiders have a decent track record at home against preseason Super Bowl contenders, losing by only a field goal to the Chiefs and Bills, but the Los Angeles Rams are 2-4 and desperate.

The Rams lost wide receiver Davante Adams and defensive tackles Kobie Turner and Poona Ford to injuries. Yet the Raiders may not be able to capitalize on those absences.

Expect Los Angeles to use multiple tight ends to compensate for losing Adams. The Raiders have allowed six touchdowns to tight ends this season. On another note, Las Vegas is struggling to run the ball with the 30th-ranked ground attack while giving up the fifth-most rushing yards.

The Rams snap out of a funk behind Puka Nacua, a physical ground attack featuring Kyren Williams and Blake Corum and a slew of tight ends to win by at least a touchdown.

Raiders: Davenport, Hanford, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Green Bay Packers (4-2) at Detroit Lions (3-2)

This game could be what Packers-Cowboys should have been last week if Dak Prescott and the Dallas offense had come to play. An improved Green Bay defense contributed to Dallas' struggles, but I don't see Jared Goff and Detroit struggling the same way.

With Jahmyr Gibbs to set the pace for the Lions, I like Goff to attack Green Bay's secondary more efficiently than Prescott was able to. The Lions' defense has plenty of holes as well, though. I don't see either team stopping the other very often in this one. Both teams clear 30 points, but the Lions win by a little more than a field goal at the end.

Theoretically, the bye week should help the Lions a bit defensively. The extra time to game plan for a well-known divisional rival certainly won't hurt a defense giving up nearly 30 points per game. But the Packers, while definitely not looking great, are finding ways to win. This game will almost certainly be a shootout decided by the final possession. That being the case, take the points.

Packers: Davenport, Knox, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Kansas City Chiefs (5-0) at Seattle Seahawks (3-3)

One thing we know for sure about the Seahawks is that they're resilient. This is a well-coached team that is very unlikely to lose three in a row for the first time in more than two years.

Coming off a Thursday night game in Week 6, the Seahawks have had extra time to prepare for this home game.

Sam Darnold's turnover problems are a concern heading into a matchup with Steve Spagnuolo's defense. The Seattle Seahawks' starter is tied for second in the NFL with seven interceptions despite playing fewer than five full games.

The Seahawks, meanwhile, are haunted by the fact that they let the Super Bowl MVP join the Kansas City Chiefs in the offseason and reemerge as a viable regular-season MVP candidate while their own ground game runs in neutral.

It's always tough to pick against Seattle at home in prime time, but only one of these teams has looked and played like a legitimate Super Bowl threat this season, and it hasn't been the defending champs.

Chiefs: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Dallas Cowboys (2-4) at Philadelphia Eagles (2-4)

The NFC East is a weird place, especially in prime time. The Eagles' season may be imploding, but that's not enough for me to back the extremely untrustworthy Cowboys as a sizeable road favorite against an experienced and resilient opponent that is very familiar with everything Dallas does. Both teams are messes, so this feels like a field-goal game.

I should take the points in this one. The Eagles being at a crossroads will probably spark a strong performance from the home side in this prime time NFC East rivalry, and the smart play is to take the points. The Dallas defense is third-worst in the league in yards allowed per game (382.5) and eighth-worst in points per game (26.5).

But the Eagles haven't figured things out offensively at all and average only 17.7 points per game. Only the Dolphins, Titans, Chargers and Browns are worse at scoring points right now. Dak Prescott and the Cowboys offense can be formidable when things go well, and the o-line has surrendered only seven sacks this season.

The NFC East is wide open, and while it pains me something fierce to say it, the Dallas offense is the division's best unit and could shine in the spotlight. At less than a touchdown, I'll roll the dice on a big game from Dak, CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens in a must-win game.

articles.title: The Rams are in serious trouble, a showdown in Seattle and a trip to Paris: Here’s what to watch in the NFL’s Week 7
articles.summary: Six weeks into the NFL season, some preseason Super Bowl favorites are already fighting to keep their playoff hopes alive, while a few divisions are making a strong case for being the worst in football.
articles.body: Six weeks into the NFL season, some preseason Super Bowl favorites are already fighting to keep their playoff hopes alive, while a few divisions are making a strong case for being the worst in football. With the Los Angeles Rams approaching panic mode, the NFC East in complete disarray and the Kansas City Chiefs preparing for their biggest test yet, there’s no shortage of drama heading into Week 7. Here are the five things to know for the games ahead. Rams watching the panic meter This season certainly hasn’t gone according to plan for the Rams. Sunday’s shocking loss to the Arizona Cardinals dropped Los Angeles to 2-4, and, suddenly, a team that entered the season with Super Bowl aspirations is fighting to stay in the playoff picture. Last week, I said it wasn’t time to panic just yet. Well, we’re getting dangerously close to sounding the alarm. The Rams’ next four games are at the Las Vegas Raiders, home against the Los Angeles Chargers, and away at both the Washington Commanders and the Cardinals. On paper, that’s a favorable stretch, but LA has almost no room for error. The Rams may need to run the table because the schedule gets considerably tougher after that. With the San Francisco 49ers off to a perfect 6-0 start and threatening to run away with the NFC West, the Rams may already be playing for a wild card spot. If 10 wins is the target, Los Angeles would need to go 8-3 over its final 11 games. That’s certainly possible, but the Rams haven’t shown much through six games to suggest they’re capable of that kind of run. The Rams entered the season as the Super Bowl favorites at +500. Those odds have since slipped to +1200, although they’re still among the top five favorites to win it all. History hasn’t exactly been kind to overwhelming preseason favorites. Teams that have been that favored at +500 or better to start the season are 0-20 over the last 30 years when it comes to winning it all. So far, that stat looks like it’s going to continue to hold up. NFC Least Remember when the NFC East was considered one of the NFL’s premier divisions? Those days feel like a distant memory. Right now, the NFC East is battling the NFC South for the title of worst division in football, and the last two weeks have been particularly ugly. The NFC East became the first division in NFL history to have all four teams play in a two-week span and nobody win. The New York Giants and Commanders even played each other! Perhaps the most telling sign of how bad things have gotten is that the 2-4 Dallas Cowboys are currently favored to win the division. Yes, the same Cowboys who have looked downright awful in their four losses. The Philadelphia Eagles, meanwhile, are expected to be without quarterback Jalen Hurts for the rest of the season as he deals with a serious medical issue involving blood clots. Then there are the Giants, who are turning to JJ McCarthy in hopes of providing a spark at quarterback. McCarthy was thrown straight into the fire against the Saints and managed to throw for 243 yards in just 11 minutes of action. Now, he’ll get his first start Sunday in Houston, where New York enters as a 10-point underdog against a Texans team that’s just 2-4 itself. The good news? Somebody in the NFC East is guaranteed to avoid a loss this week when the Eagles host the Cowboys on Monday Night Football. Of course, they could always tie. And that might be the most fitting outcome for this division. Bonjour, NFL! Set those alarms early again Sunday because the NFL is headed overseas for another international showdown. But this time, we’re trading London for Paris. For the first time ever, the NFL is scheduled to play a regular-season game in the City of Light, with the Pittsburgh Steelers taking on the New Orleans Saints at 9:30 a.m. ET. League officials say heightened security measures will be in place following recent civil unrest in Paris. The matchup is part of the NFL’s expanded international schedule, which features nine games outside the United States this season. And the league’s global tour is far from over. November will bring three more international matchups: The Atlanta Falcons and Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid, Spain; the Detroit Lions and New England Patriots in Munich, Germany; and the 49ers and Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City. Chiefs’ toughest test yet Are the Kansas City Chiefs really as good as their undefeated record suggests? We’re about to find out. Patrick Mahomes and company are taking their perfect record to Seattle for a Sunday Night Football showdown against the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks. And this will easily be their biggest test of the season. That’s because Kansas City’s five victories haven’t exactly come against a murderer’s row of opponents. The Chiefs have beaten a Denver Broncos team that was still finding its footing, the 2-4 Indianapolis Colts, the winless Miami Dolphins, a respectable Raiders squad and the 0-6 Chargers. Combined, that’s not exactly an intimidating résumé. Unfortunately for Kansas City, they are catching an angry Seahawks team. Mike Macdonald’s squad is coming off back-to-back losses to the Niners and Broncos, their first consecutive defeats since December 2024. For Seattle, this is a chance to remind everyone why it’s the defending champion. For Kansas City, it’s an opportunity to prove that its perfect start is about more than a favorable schedule. A much-needed bye Four teams have the week off: the Buffalo Bills, Commanders, Chargers and Jacksonville Jaguars. And while Buffalo and Jacksonville can use the break to rest and recharge, fans in Washington and Los Angeles are hoping a week away might somehow fix what’s gone wrong. For Commanders coach Dan Quinn and Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh, the pressure is mounting. Both coaches appear likely to survive the bye week, which hasn’t always been a guarantee for struggling NFL teams. The midseason break has historically been a convenient time for organizations to make a coaching change, giving an interim replacement extra time to prepare. Washington at least has one thing working in its favor: The NFC East is so bad that the Commanders still have a realistic path back into the division race. The Chargers? Well, things are looking considerably more bleak. At this point, Chargers fans might want to spend their bye week firing up the mock draft simulator and figuring out how to fix this team next season. articles.title: NFL analyst says it's 'difficult to explain' who the Falcons are
articles.summary: NFL analyst says it's 'difficult to explain' who the Falcons are this season
articles.body:
It's been an up and down kind of season for the Atlanta Falcons so far. After two humiliating losses they reeled off two dominant wins, followed by two more frustrating losses.

Which version of these Falcons is the real one? That's anybody's guess going into Week 7, where they'll face the best team in the NFL, the 6-0 San Francisco 49ers.

For what it's worth Nick Shook at NFL.com has Atlanta at No. 19 in his latest power rankings , down four spots from last week. He doesn't seem to know what to make of these Falcons, and it's tough to blame him.

"...With Atlanta sitting at 2-4, it's difficult to explain who these Falcons are. They've turned in two wildly impressive showings, let a win slip through their fingers in Week 5 and were largely dominated by a hungry Bears team at home. More tests await, too: San Francisco, Tampa Bay, Cincinnati and Kansas City are the next four opponents. We'll learn plenty about this squad in the coming month."

While it's tough to know what to expect going into any given matchup, the winning formula is pretty obvious. The Falcons have to establish an early lead, enabling them to ride Bijan Robinson and an aggressive defense to victory. If they fall behind early, then they have to rely on Michael Penix Jr., who's just not ready to carry a team from behind yet.

Shook is right that we will learn a lot about this team over the next four weeks. If they can manage to split these games and go 2-2 it will be a good sign for the rest of their season.

articles.title: Lions Week 7 preview: Breaking down Packers’ offensive, defensive schemes
articles.summary: Breaking down the offensive and defensive schemes of the Green Bay Packers the Detroit Lions’ Week 7 opponent.
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions (3-2) and Green Bay Packers (4-2) will square off in Detroit's first NFC North battle of the 2026 season.

"They're playing really good football right now," Lions coach Dan Campbell said of the Packers. "Two of their best games have been these back-to-back games. Plus-six in the turnover ratio the last two weeks; it was seven takeaways on defense, man. It's an opportunistic defense. They fly around the football. They disguise well and create issues. […] it's been an outstanding test for us. Hell of an opponent, first division game of the season at home. We're looking forward to it, but this is a real good team right now playing good football."

Let's take a closer look at the Packers' coaching staff, the scheme they run, and scouting notes from their most recently viewed games.

NFL coaching seasons: 18th (Texans, Washington, Falcons, Rams, Titans, Packers) Head coaching seasons : 8th (Packers 2019-present) Offensive coordinator : 2nd (Rams 2017, Titans 2018) Other coaching roles held : QB coach, Offensive assistant Influences: Mike Shanahan, Kyle Shanahan, and Sean McVay Coached under: Both Shanahans, McVay, Gary Kubiak, Dan Quinn, Mike Vrabel Play caller : Yes

"Matt's (LaFleur) doing a hell of a job. They have. They've gotten better every week. […] what Matt's done over there and they've done offensively, they've evolved in areas, but there are some things that they're going to hang their hat on. They're good at and they're not going to change that. They'll just wrinkle it, man, a bunch of eye candy to try to get you off of it. And it's effective. It's still effective. It's been effective every year."

NFL coaching seasons : 10th (49ers, Packers) Offensive coordinator seasons : 5th (Packers 2022-present) Previous coaching positions : Run game coordinator, OL coach, Assistant OL coach Playing career : 5 seasons on NFL practice squads (Panthers, Packers, Cowboys, Texans) Influences: Kyle Shanahan and Matt LaFleur Coached under: Shanahan and LaFleur

Primarily utilize 11-personnel: 60% of the time — 12-personnel: 25%; 13-personnel: 15%

Efficient passing attack — 269.3 passing yards per game (5th)

Have moved the ball well; struggled to score touchdowns early in the season, but have improved

Pass yards per play: 7.5 (12th); EPA per pass: 0.05 (13th)

Red zone touchdown efficiency: 50% (22nd); Jordan Love EPA in red zone: -0.24 (32nd)

3rd most explosive passing plays in the NFL

The deep ball also leads to big penalties; gained 135 yards on penalties on deep passes through six games

Majority of all targets go to top three skill players: WR Matthew Golden, WR Christian Watson, TE Tucker Kraft

Target share: Golden 26%, Watson 22%, Kraft 17% — That's two-thirds of the passes thrown by Love

Offensive line play has been an issue, both in the pass and run game

Pressures allowed: 97 (29th); pressure rate: 40.2% (25th); quick pressure rate 22.1% (22nd)

Jordan Love EPA when pressured: -0.26 (17th), per Sumer Sports

Run game has been, by far, the worst rushing attack in the NFL

OL stats: PFF blocking grade: 47.3 (32nd); DVOA (32); adjusted yards (32nd)

RB Josh Jacobs is eligible to return, and while the Packers are playing coy, the Lions say they expect him to play — but how ready will he be after not playing football for the last month and a half?

"They've settled some things in in that old line. […] (QB Jordan) Love, man. He makes it go. He is the secret sauce. And (WR Christian) Watson and (WR Matthew) Golden, man, they're dangerous threats down the field and he's going to give them opportunities that shows up every week. (TE Tucker) Kraft has come off the injury nicely. He's gotten better every week. He's playing good football right now. So, this team's playing at a high level."

NFL coaching seasons : 16th (Falcons, Titans, Vikings, Colts, Eagles, Cardinals, Packers) Defensive coordinator seasons : 3rd (Eagles 2021-22, Packers 2026) Head coaching seasons : 3 seasons (Cardinals 2022-25) Previous roles : DB coach, assistant DB coach, defensive quality control; Scout (Rams 2009-11) Influences: Mike Zimmer, Matt Eberflus, Vic Fangio Coached under: Zimmer, Eberflus, Jerry Gray, Emmitt Thomas; Nick Sirianni, Frank Reich, Bobby Petrino Staff ties to Detroit : Daniel Bullocks (Packers CB coach — drafted by Detroit in the second round of the 2006 NFL Draft)

Rotate four defensive tackles through 3- and 2-down DL fronts
